Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-01 15:00 UTC

Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya K. (CTO), Evan S. (NetEng), Ruth M. (Sec Arch), Daniel K. (Platform)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: ok great thanks everyone for jumping on, uh this is a workshop to map out network constraints for the private deployment, we'll try to cover peering, private endpoints, and region gating.
[00:23] Priya: thanks Maya. quick note - our timeline is Q3 pilot, production by end Q4, but the blocker rn is network and egress policy sign off.
[00:35] Omar: understood. can you walk us through how your VPCs are arranged today? any transit gateways or central egress?
[00:48] Evan: yeah we have a hub-and-spoke with TGW in us-east-1 and us-west-2. on prem connects via Direct Connect to the hub. most app traffic goes out through a centralized NAT in the hub, so egress IPs are static-ish but tied to those NAT gateways.
[01:12] Ruth: and from security perspective we need predictable egress IPs for allowlists, plus audit logs for any model inference payloads that touch PII.
[01:27] Daniel: small correction: not all tenants route through the hub, some dev VPCs still peer directly for latency.
[01:39] Maya: ok that helps. Redwood Private supports multiple connectivity patterns - TGW, VPC peering, and private endpoints. usually we recommend private endpoints for minimal surface area but if you need cross-region low latency peering we can do peering or TGW routing.
[02:05] Evan: one big question - can Redwood accept traffic from our NATed egress IPs so we can keep the allowlist on our firewall? or do we have to punch holes inbound?
[02:18] Omar: you can use private endpoints (privatelink) so the traffic stays inside AWS, but for outbound allowlisting if you want predictable egress IPs we can place a small egress proxy within your VPC that front-ends requests to Redwood; that proxy would present static IPs. there's also an option to run in your private deployment with no public IPs - all traffic via VPC endpoint.
[02:45] Priya: oh right the egress proxy idea — does that add latency?
[02:47] Omar: negligible, usually a few tens of ms depending on region and path, we can include perf numbers from similar customers.
[03:03] Ruth: we need encryption in transit and at rest, also keys must be under our KMS. does Redwood support bringing your own key (BYOK) or HSM integration when Private is deployed?
[03:16] Maya: yes for Private we offer KMS integration, you can bring keys and we will configure the control plane to use customer-managed KMS for secrets. Omar can cover the HSM nuances.
[03:28] Omar: technically we integrate with AWS KMS CMKs and can have the data plane use envelope encryption with customer keys. if you want on-prem HSM talk to our security team - it's possible but extra steps. also audit logs are available - we can stream them to your S3 or to a SIEM via secure forwarder.
[03:52] Evan: good. about regions - do you host inference in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1? we have data residency constraints in eu and apac for certain customers.
[04:06] Maya: we currently support eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 in Private; for hosted there might be differences. for Dedicated/Private you can pick allowed regions. we'll note that your EU tenant needs to stay in eu-west-1.
[04:23] Daniel: if we pin the model to a region, is there automatic fallback to other regions in case of outage?
[04:30] Omar: standard behavior is we don't cross-region replica unless configured; you can set a fallback policy to route to a warm standby in another region but that'll raise latency and compliance considerations.
[04:45] Priya: what about CIDR collisions - we often see peering fail because of overlapping private ranges. what's Redwood's recommendation?
[04:54] Maya: we ask for non-overlapping /16 or /20 depending on scale. we can also put a NAT or proxy in the middle to avoid direct peering if overlap exists, but it's simpler to reassign the customer CIDR.
[05:11] Evan: we can provide our CIDR list. also firewall team wants the list of Redwood egress IPs if any - do you provide static egress IPs for the service?
[05:22] Omar: for Private deployments, Redwood runs in your VPC so the egress IPs are controlled by you. for Hosted we provide a published set of egress IPs, but for Private it's under customer control.
[05:36] Ruth: perfect. next, can we get sample security docs - like SOC2, pen test results, and any hardening checklist for the control plane?
[05:46] Maya: yes we'll attach SOC2 report and an infra hardening checklist. note some docs have redactions, but we'll provide what's shareable.
[05:55] Priya: on SSO - we use SAML idp (Okta) and need RBAC mapped to groups. can Redwood integrate into our SAML and map groups to roles?
[06:06] Omar: yes SAML SSO is supported, we can map groups to roles and support SCIM provisioning too.
[06:16] Evan: one outage scenario - if TGW in us-east-1 fails, can we route to the other region over peering? any recommended pattern to avoid blackholing?
[06:27] Omar: common pattern is active-active with health checks and a regional failover policy. also we recommend monitoring hooks and can emit traces to your tracing backend.
[06:40] Daniel: do you support cross-account privatelink where the endpoint service is in a Redwood account and we accept connections?
[06:48] Maya: yes we can publish a privatelink service for your account to subscribe to; that flow requires Accept of the endpoint and sometimes whitelisting. it's pretty standard.
[07:00] Priya: curious about billing and egress costs - if traffic stays in our VPC via privatelink is there data processing charge?
[07:10] Omar: privatelink has data processing fees on AWS side and there may be charges for the endpoint itself. Redwood also charges per-inference usage; we can provide a cost model for your traffic estimate.
[07:26] Evan: we'd like to run a lab - can you spin up a test private endpoint and we will run a connectivity test using our firewall rules?
[07:34] Maya: yes we can provision a short-lived endpoint for lab. Omar will run the test and collect logs.
[07:40] Omar: noted. i'll need the CIDR ranges and the security team contact for firewall rules.
[07:47] Ruth: it's Ruth.Mercado@nebulaworks.com - i'll coordinate.
[07:52] Maya: great. a few gotchas: if you use strict egress IP whitelisting and also want BYOK, make sure routing doesn't force traffic out to an internet egress path that changes IPs; test early. also KV cache persistence across restarts - sometimes customers want the KV cache to remain in same region for perf.
[08:12] Evan: KV cash? i think you mean K V cache — transcription error, but yes we care about KV cache locality.
[08:18] Maya: (laughs) yes KV cache. we can pin caches to region to avoid cross-region fetches.
[08:24] Priya: one more question: does Redwood collect logs containing request payloads, and can we disable payload persistence?
[08:32] Omar: for Private deployments, you control log retention. by default we emit metadata-only logs to the control plane but we can disable payload capture. we'll document the exact flags.
[08:45] Daniel: excellent. do you have a checklist for network onboarding?
[08:50] Maya: yes i'll share our onboarding checklist which includes required CIDRs, SG rules, route table entries, privatelink accept steps, and required firewall rules.
[08:58] Priya: ok let's recap and agree next steps.
[09:02] Maya: recap - Redwood to share diagrams, SOC2 + KMS docs, propose CIDR ranges for peering, provision a lab endpoint next week, NebulaWorks to send CIDRs and firewall owner, security to confirm data residency constraints.
[09:20] Priya: sounds good. any blockers from your side Omar?
[09:24] Omar: no blockers, just need the info. i'll prepare a short runbook for the lab test.
[09:30] Ruth: also we may require an on-call rotation for the week of the lab in case we hit firewall issues.
[09:37] Maya: noted, i'll include contact fields for that.
[09:40] Evan: timeframe - can we run the lab next Tue or Wed?
[09:44] Maya: next Tue 14:00 UTC works from our side, i'll propose in calendar.
[09:49] Priya: ok great thanks everyone.
[09:51] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and the calendar invite.
